explanations.answer: His disciples and a large crowd
explanations.explanation: Luke says, "His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd." (Luke 7:11) So Jesus isn't walking alone. That's a whole parade heading toward Nain. I walk with a crowd only when somebody smells a fresh batch.

Close, but the text doesn't name just two. Luke says, "His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd." (Luke 7:11) That's more than two guys and a quiet stroll. Peter and John aren't even named in this passage.

Luke doesn't mention any Pharisees or scribes on this road. He says, "His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd." (Luke 7:11) So the road to Nain is full of disciples and crowd. A few more folks in the group chat, you could say, but not those folks.

Luke says he is "the only son of his mother." (Luke 7:12) That's one son, and he's the one being carried out. I think that makes the scene even heavier. This is a hard moment, and Luke doesn't rush past it.
Luke doesn't count him as a second son. He says the dead man is "the only son of his mother." (Luke 7:12) No older brother in the picture here. That's one son, and he's the one in the coffin.
Not a third son. Luke says the dead man is "the only son of his mother." (Luke 7:12) There's no line of brothers here. I think that tells us how heavy this day is for her.

It's the other way around. Luke says the dead man was the only son of his mother, "and she was a widow." (Luke 7:12) A widow is a woman whose husband has died. So her husband is gone, and now her only son is too. I think she's carrying more than anybody should.

Right. Luke says the dead man was "the only son of his mother, and she was a widow." (Luke 7:12) A widow's husband has died. So she has no husband, and her only son is the one being carried out. I think this is a heavy part of the story.
Luke says, "When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her." (Luke 7:13) He sees her first, and compassion comes right away. Nobody had to ask Him. Friend, that's the whole tone of this scene.
No questions from Jesus here. Luke says, "When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her." (Luke 7:13) He sees her and compassion is what He has. No interview, no paperwork.

No warnings. Luke says, "When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her." (Luke 7:13) A woman walking behind her son's coffin doesn't need a lecture. Jesus gives her compassion, and that's what the text says.

Jesus says to her, "Do not weep." (Luke 7:13) Those are His words to a mother in the middle of a funeral. Think about that for a second. A line like that could sound empty from anyone else, but the story is about to show who's saying it.
Jesus does say that to people in other places, but not here. Here He tells the widow, "Do not weep." (Luke 7:13) She's grieving, and that's what He speaks to. Good line, wrong scene, baker.

That's a line Jesus uses at other times, like when He speaks to a woman in Luke 7:50. Here, though, He tells the widow, "Do not weep." (Luke 7:13) He speaks right to her sorrow. The words fit her moment exactly.

The men stop. Luke says, "Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still." (Luke 7:14) Jesus touches it and the whole procession halts. Imagine carrying a coffin and a stranger just walks up and touches it. I'd be frozen too, and I'm bolted to a gold base.

Right, they don't keep walking. Luke says, "Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still." (Luke 7:14) The whole procession stops. I bet nobody in that line knew what was coming next.

explanations.answer: The young man in the coffin
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, "Young man, I tell you, get up!" (Luke 7:14) He speaks right to the one in the coffin. Most people would talk to the mourners. Jesus talks to the one everybody else had given up on hearing anything.
The disciples aren't the ones He's talking to. Jesus says, "Young man, I tell you, get up!" (Luke 7:14) He turns to the one in the coffin. The disciples are just there for the show.

The men carrying it have already stood still. Then Jesus says, "Young man, I tell you, get up!" (Luke 7:14) He's speaking to the one in the coffin, not to them. I think those men were just trying to hold on to that coffin.

It happens just like that. Luke says, "the dead man sat up and began to speak!" (Luke 7:15) Jesus speaks, and the young man sits up. He doesn't just sit up, he starts talking. I'd love to know what a first word like that sounds like, but the text doesn't tell us.
It does happen. Luke says, "the dead man sat up and began to speak!" (Luke 7:15) After Jesus says, "get up!" the young man sits up and talks. Nobody in that crowd had a plan for this part.

Luke says, "Then Jesus gave him back to his mother." (Luke 7:15) She's the widow who walked behind that coffin. Now her son is standing in front of her. I think that's the moment the whole story has been heading toward.
No master in this story. Luke says, "Then Jesus gave him back to his mother." (Luke 7:15) She's the widow from the funeral. That's who gets her son back.

No brothers here. Luke says he's "the only son of his mother" (Luke 7:12), and then "Jesus gave him back to his mother." (Luke 7:15) He goes right back to her. A mother who had no one else gets her son.

Luke says, "A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God." (Luke 7:16) Awe is that stunned feeling you get when something is bigger than you. They walked out for a funeral and got this instead. I think their mouths were hanging open.
No anger here. Luke says, "A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God." (Luke 7:16) Nobody storms off. They're too stunned and too busy praising God.

Doubt doesn't win this one. Luke says, "A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God." (Luke 7:16) The young man is sitting up and talking, so there's not much left to argue about. Awe is what sweeps over them.

They say, "A great prophet has appeared among us!" (Luke 7:16) A prophet is someone who speaks for God. That's what the people say when they see this happen. They also say, "God has visited His people!"
Not king. The people say, "A great prophet has appeared among us!" (Luke 7:16) That's the word they use. A prophet is someone who speaks for God.
Not judge. The people say, "A great prophet has appeared among us!" (Luke 7:16) A prophet is someone who speaks for God. That's the word that came out of the crowd that day.

It doesn't stay put. Luke says, "the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region." (Luke 7:17) That's a lot of ground for one town's news. I can't even keep a batch secret from my own bakery.

Right, it doesn't stay in Nain. Luke says, "the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region." (Luke 7:17) Judea is the region around Jerusalem. That's way past the town gate.
